decisions.description: Withdrawals are capped at 5000 per account per day, a limit the plan never mentions.
The 'daily' withdrawal counter is never reset, so it really works as a lifetime cap of 5000 per account.
The withdrawal limit applies only to withdrawals; transfers out are not counted and have no limit.
Amounts are rounded to cents with Math.round (half-up, on binary floating point), which the plan does not specify.
Rounding happens after the positivity check, so an amount like 0.001 passes validation and is recorded as a zero-value operation.
Balances and amounts are stored as floating-point numbers rather than integer cents.
The positivity check rejects NaN but accepts Infinity, so an infinite amount is a valid deposit.
A repeated transaction id returns success and is silently ignored, without checking that account, amount or operation type match the original.
Transaction ids are unique across all accounts and all operation types, so the same id used for a deposit blocks an unrelated withdrawal.
A transaction id is only remembered when the operation succeeds, so a rejected operation can be retried with the same id and later succeed.
Amount validation runs before the duplicate check, so a retry with an invalid amount is rejected instead of acknowledged.
Accounts are created implicitly on first use by any operation, with no explicit opening or existence check.
A rejected withdrawal or transfer still creates the account(s) it referenced.
Asking for the balance of an unknown account returns 0 instead of an error.
Asking for the history of an unknown account returns an empty list instead of an error.
New accounts start with a balance of 0.
Overdrafts are not allowed: withdrawals and transfers that would take a balance below zero are rejected.
In a withdrawal, insufficient funds is checked before the daily limit, so that reason wins when both apply.
Rejected operations are not recorded anywhere in the history.
History records the rounded amount, not the amount the client sent.
A transfer is recorded as two entries, transfer-out and transfer-in, sharing the same transaction id, with no link to the counterparty account.
Rejection reasons are fixed strings: invalid-amount, insufficient-funds and daily-limit.
Account ids and transaction ids are not validated, so empty or arbitrary strings are accepted.
History entries carry no timestamp.
